The Weekend Guide

This Weekend in the Bay

Friday 21 – Sunday 23 August 2026

A quarter-century of electronic music marked in one night in the Mission, seventy-five thousand paper kites going up at SFMOMA, an avant-garde filmmaker threading his own 16mm in Berkeley, and eleven hours of experimental sound on a farm above the Pacific. A quiet weekend for gallery receptions and an unusually loud one for the strange stuff.

Clear skies Fri & Sat — telescope nights are on SFEMF turns 25 Free Saturday at the de Young & Legion Brackens closes at YBCA Three sold-out shows at BAMPFA

Top 5 This Weekend

If you only do five things — one from each corner of the calendar.

  1. SFEMF 25th Anniversary Gala
    Sat Aug 22, 7:30pm · Gray Area, Mission
    Twenty-five years of the SF Electronic Music Festival in one night — Carl Stone and Wobbly, and Luciano Chessa reviving Ramón Sender Barayón's Desert Ambulance. The kind of anniversary that does not come round again.
  2. Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc opens
    Sat Aug 22 · SFMOMA, SoMa · free
    Seventy-five thousand hand-built kites, the largest work of the artist's career — hung in the one SFMOMA gallery you do not need a ticket for.
  3. Four Films by Jerome Hiler, in person
    Fri Aug 21, 7pm · BAMPFA, Berkeley
    Hand-made 16mm that has never been released to video and is only ever projected to the filmmaker's own standards — with the filmmaker in the room. 48 Hills' pick of the week.
  4. SECRET MAGIC at The Palace Theater
    Fri & Sat, 6:30pm · North Beach (enter through the clock shop)
    Eight magicians, eight rooms, two stage shows, and one wardrobe you walk through. Back for two nights only after selling out twice.
  5. West Edge Opera: Claude & Marcel preview
    Sun Aug 23, 3pm · SFMOMA, SoMa
    The first public orchestral hearing of a new opera about the two surrealist photographers who ran a resistance cell against the Nazis on Jersey. It does not premiere properly until 2027.

Big Museums

Exhibits, after-hours and museum one-offs

TOP PICK✦ Opens Saturday

Jacob Hashimoto: Giant Arc

Opens Sat Aug 22 · Fri–Sun 10am–5pm

SFMOMA, Roberts Family Gallery · SoMa San Francisco

Nearly 75,000 hand-built bamboo-and-paper kites massed into a floor-to-ceiling canopy — the largest work of Hashimoto's career, hung in the one SFMOMA gallery that sits outside the ticket barrier.

Free — no museum ticket needed

★ CRITICS' · Mission Local✦ US debut

Treasures of the Pharaohs

Fri–Sun · 9:30am–5:15pm (docent tour 11:30am)

de Young Museum · Golden Gate Park San Francisco

130 objects across 3,000 years, including the US debut of finds from the newly excavated Golden City near Luxor. The curator's own line: this may be your first and last chance to see this jewellery.

$40 timed ticket

★ CRITICS' · KQED · Artforum✦ Closes Sunday

Diedrick Brackens: gather tender night

Final day Sun Aug 23 · 11am–5pm

YBCA, Gallery 2 · SoMa San Francisco

Fifteen monumental hand-dyed weavings in Brackens's first Bay Area solo show. It closes Sunday, so this really is the last weekend.

$10

✦ One night only

Sci-Fi Night: Men in Black on the Planetarium Dome

Fri Aug 21 · doors 7pm, film 7:30pm

Chabot Space & Science Center · Oakland Hills East Bay

The film projected across a 70-foot planetarium dome with themed cocktails, and the observation deck open afterwards for free telescope viewing. 18+.

$20 ($10 members)

Friday Nights at OMCA with Sabrina Shauna

Fri Aug 21 · 5–9pm

Oakland Museum of California · Lake Merritt East Bay

The reliable one: Off the Grid trucks along 10th Street, live R&B on the Garden Stage at 6:30, volunteer gallery chats from 5:30, and live figure drawing in the Gallery of California Art.

Free to attend

Organ Concert: Jonathan Dimmock, The Beauty of Summer

Sat Aug 22 · 4pm

Legion of Honor · Lincoln Park San Francisco

Brewer, Brahms and Copland's Rodeo on the Skinner organ in the Rodin-lined court — and Saturday is a free-admission day for Bay Area residents.

Free with admission (free Sat for residents)

✦ First US retrospective

Lotty Rosenfeld: Disobedient Spaces

Fri–Sun · gallery hours

BAMPFA · Downtown Berkeley East Bay

The first US retrospective of the Chilean artist who spent decades laying crosses across public roads under Pinochet. Showing alongside the Maren Hassinger survey.

Included with admission

Openings, closings and studio doors

TOP PICK✦ One-off preview

West Edge Opera: Claude & Marcel — Orchestral Preview

Notes

Times were read off each venue's own event page wherever possible, not off aggregator grids. Where the two disagreed, the venue won — which is how The Soiled Dove came out of this guide (an aggregator listed it for Friday and Saturday; Vau de Vire's own ticketing shows 8/28 and 8/29), and how the World Arts West panel ended up on Saturday rather than Friday. A run of Chronicle Datebook picks turned out to have already happened — Herbie Hancock was Monday the 17th, FACT/SF was the 14th–16th, Bon Odori was in July, Going to St. Ives closed in July — so they are not here either.

Worth double-checking before you go: the Chabot telescope viewings are cancelled in high humidity — the forecast is clear for Friday and Saturday nights, but check the observatory page the day of. Barry Lyndon, 2001 and Grave of the Fireflies at BAMPFA and Jeff Parker at the Freight are all sold out, with door waitlists. Sunday Streets Bayview has not published an official start time; 12–5pm is the listed figure. Ticket prices at BAMPFA, the Stanford and the CinemaSF houses are approximate.

Deliberately left out: arena and stadium shows, DJ and club nights (which took out both DNA Lounge nights and the Saturday half of Rooftop Rhythms), beer festivals, sports, and — per the standing note for this run — Pride and LGBTQ-specific programming, which this weekend meant the SF Queer Film Festival occupying most of the Roxie, the Castro Night Market's drag stage, Monét X Change at Cobb's, and YBCA's Conjuring Power.

Scanned across all fifteen source categories in the registry, plus critics at the Chronicle, KQED, 48 Hills, Mission Local, SF Standard, 7x7, SF Classical Voice and Broke-Ass Stuart. Note that the weekend pick columns for these dates had not published yet when this was built on Monday, so the critics' badges come from reviews and previews of shows that run into the weekend rather than from a weekend round-up.
